description: On 26 September 2014, 43 students from the Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers' College were forcibly disappeared in Iguala, Guerrero. They had left to take part in a demonstration commemorating the 2 October 1968 student massacre.
energy_note: Forty-three young men, on their way to a commemoration.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the 'historical truth' was built on torture
description: The Peña Nieto government closed the case within months on confessions that the bodies were burned in a dump. International experts disputed it, citing confessions obtained by torture, illegal arrests of key suspects and absence of physical evidence. The GIEI, appointed by the IACHR in 2015, rejected the cremation theory as physically impossible as described.
energy_note: The official story was produced by torturing people.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the state later admitted it was a state crime
description: The truth commission report released on 18 August 2022 conceded the disappearance was a 'state crime' involving local officials and military units, and that the previous government pursued deliberate concealment and obstruction. Critics noted it did not address the roles of SEDENA, the military command or CISEN.
energy_note: Admitted as a state crime, with the state's own part left out.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and the files are still being fought for
description: The GIEI completed its work on 31 July 2023. A federal judge ruled the army must make public 853 files obtained in 2014 by the Regional Intelligence Fusion Center, after parents filed an amparo in 2023 against the military for violating the 2018 decree creating the truth commission.
energy_note: Twelve years on, still suing for the documents.

aspect: Nine years on, the IACHR recorded nothing resolved
description: Whereabouts not determined, facts not fully clarified, those responsible not punished. The most internationally scrutinised disappearance in Mexican history is unsolved - which sets the expectation for all the others.
energy_note: If this one is unsolved, none of them will be.
